thread:
anna: heads up — customer-rep (acct: acct-221) seeing intermittent 504s on hosted API /v1/stream (realtime chat). ~3 hits in last 10m, all mid-stream. trace ids: trc-2c9a, trc-7b4f

jess: got it. are these guest tokens or dedicated customers? any common region?
	anna: guest; us-west1. payloads are small (single prompt) but client keeps long poll open for SSE streaming.
	mike: quick check of ingress logs shows repeated entries "upstream response timeout" from envoy on the edge nodes around those traces.
	sre-bot: alert created: #INC-2026-332 — edge/ingress upstream_timeout spikes, avg 30s for affected traces.
	anna: reproduction attempt from my laptop (us-west) — intermittent, but I can trigger a 504 reliably by curl with small sleep between bytes. sample: 

	```bash	curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer GUEST_TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
	  -d '{"model":"r-instruct-2","prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream --no-buffer	```

	when I chunk the body slowly (cat with sleep) I get a 504 after ~32s.
	jess: interesting. that points to idle/flow-control issues on the edge h2 pools. not classic auth rotation.
	mike: checking envoy config: route timeout is 30s for that route (we set conservative default recently). streaming endpoints should be 0 (infinite) or much higher.
	anna: oh — we did a policy change last week to apply a global 30s route timeout to reduce stuck upstreams. guess it hit streaming.
	ryan-cs: customer is seeing user-facing failures in prod, wants ETA. can we hotfix?
	jess: short term: set route timeout to 60s for /v1/stream and mark streaming routes with disable_idle_timeout. I can push a small canary change.
	mike: agree. also need to ensure envoy idle timeout and upstream idle_window settings align — h2 window drift causes early upstream reset even when backend still generating.
	sre-bot: suggested mitigation steps logged in INC-2026-332: bump route timeout, enable per-route streaming flag, add retry policy 503->retry with small backoff.
	anna: I'm going to run a quick canary: update ingress route timeout for path /v1/stream to 60s on two nodes only. will post deploy id.
	deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/ingress-route-timeout-1765432205 -> nodes edge-12, edge-23.
	anna: canary deployed. run your curl repro now?
	mike: ran curl 5x in a row with slow chunking — no 504s so far (30s previously, now nothing after 60s). traces: trc-a1b2, trc-a1b3 show continuous upstream stream.
	anna: good sign. will roll to remaining nodes in 5m pending no regressions.
	jess: follow-up: ops/infra should add a rule to exclude SSE/streaming endpoints from the global 30s policy. I'll open a PR for route annotations + unit tests.
	mike: also adding logging for "upstream response timeout" correlation to identify other routes accidentally covered.
	ryan-cs: customer updated: thanks, they see fewer errors but will monitor.
	anna: postmortem action items added to INC-2026-332: (1) revert global 30s route timeout default for streaming paths, (2) add e2e test that simulates chunked client bodies to detect timeout regressions, (3) update runbook for 504 mid-stream: check route timeout, envoy upstream_idle, h2 window stats, and trace ids.
	jess: one more note — if we see similar but only for large headers, check metadata header size + proxy buffer settings. not the case here.
	mike: closing loop: rolling to remaining edges now. will update incident when fully rolled.
	deploy-bot: deploy success: canary -> full rollout complete at 1765432268.
	anna: rollback window passed, no new 504 reports in 20m. marking incident as mitigated; keeping open for monitoring 24h. :thumbsup:
